Priya: Hey creative — we’re rolling a compact launch for the MicroSeq mini-benchmark + companion webinar (target webinar date Apr 6). Need a tidy, production-ready asset kit by EOD Apr 1 so growth and content can prep pages + ads. Deliverables below. Please confirm feasibility and rough ETA by EOD today.

Marisol: Got it. Quick Qs: can you confirm the comparison models/metrics we’ll show in the sparkline and whether you want real-number callouts or relative index values? Also who owns speaker headshots for the hero?

Priya: Models: Redwood-XS, RLHF-Tiny, and OpenFront-3. Metrics: median latency (ms), cost per 1k tokens, and 95th pct latency as a small rubric. Use relative index for the sparkline (0-100) + optional numeric tooltip for slide/table. Speaker art: Sam will drop headshots in the Figma file.

Sam: Dropping headshots and short bios into the Figma link now: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/MicroSeq-Launch. Also adding microcopy variants for social (3 x 1-line options) + webinar CTAs.

Priya: Topline deliverables: 
- Webinar hero: 1920x1080 static PNG + 6s motion loop MP4 (H.264), also reduced GIF for email.
- Social tiles: 1200x1200 (instagram), 1200x628 (linkedin), 600x600 variant for paid.
- Benchmark sparkline: export as SVG (accessible colors) + 2 PNG sizes for fallback. Include tooltip frames for slides.
- Slide master: 3x PPTX/Google Slides masters (title, data, speaker) 16:9, with interchangeable model comparison component.
- One-pager: A4 & US Letter PDF, press-ready (PDF/A preferred).
- Figma component library: tokens for colors, spacing, typography; annotated usage notes.
- Localization: layered text only (no flattened bitmaps) for en/es/fr.

Brand/legal notes: Avoid absolute superlatives like "fastest" or "cheapest" without Anya sign-off. Use the approved color token --redwood-500 for accents. Accessibility: AA contrast for all text, alt text for images, and SVGs for charts.

Marisol: Thanks — rough timing: hero motion + static (2 days), sparkline + SVG variants (1 day), slides + 1-pager (1.5 days), figma library (1 day). If I sequence, I can deliver an initial pass by Mar 28 and final pack Apr 1. Need final copy and headshots by EOD Mar 26.

Leo: For the website dev handoff, can we get export naming conventions and a small deliverable checklist (sizes + filenames)? Also request transparent backgrounds for any overlay elements.

Marisol: Yep — I’ll export optimised web variants and include an assets.json manifest. Example naming convention I’ll follow:

```
microseq_webhero_v1.mp4
microseq_webhero_v1.png
microseq_sparkline_v1.svg
microseq_sparkline_v1@2x.png
microseq_social_1200x1200_v1.png
microseq_slidemaster_title_v1.pptx
microseq_1pager_v1.pdf
```

Marisol: Export specs (quick):
- Web hero: 1920x1080, 72dpi, MP4 H.264 baseline, H.264 levels for max compatibility.
- Social: 1200x1200 PNG (sRGB) + 2x retina PNG.
- Sparkline: SVG with CSS variables for colors; fallback PNG 1200x300.
- Slides: embed fonts (Inter/Source Serif), provide PPTX + Google Slides link.
- 1-pager: PDF/A, crop marks, CMYK for press.

Anya: Quick legal check: wording guidance — avoid phrases like "lowest cost inference" or "industry-leading latency" unless you can cite our public benchmark page with the specific test harness. For landing/social, prefer "optimized for low-latency inference" or "cost-efficient inference". If you want a stronger claim we need the test methodology + numbers and my sign-off.

Priya: Noted — we’ll use "optimized for low-latency inference" and attach methodology link to the post. Sam, update social captions to the tempered language and include link to methodology.

Sam: Updated captions in Figma, pushed to the file under /copy/social-variants. Examples: 
- Option A: "MicroSeq: optimized for low-latency inference — see how we compare."
- Option B: "Lower latency, smarter routing. Join the MicroSeq webinar Apr 6."
- Option C: "Tune inference for cost and speed — register for the MicroSeq demo."

DesignBot: Automated export checklist created and attached to Figma file. Exports queued: hero (MP4, PNG), tiles (PNG x3), sparkline (SVG + PNG), slides (PPTX export), 1-pager (PDF/A). Manifest URL: https://assets.redwood-inference.com/microseq/manifest.json

Leo: Perfect. For web we’ll need an additional 16:9 hero at 1280x720 for low-bandwidth pages. Can we add that to the export list?

Marisol: Added 1280x720 hero and a 600x338 compressed variant for email hero.

Priya: Thanks all. Final asks before handoff:
- Marisol: initial pass by Mar 28 (A/B hero + sparkline).
- Sam: push final copy + headshots by Mar 26.
- Anya: legal sign-off on copy by Mar 30.
- Leo: confirm dev slot for integration Apr 2-4.

Marisol: On it — will post the initial frames in this thread when ready. :eyes: 

Sam: Will drop headshots + final microcopy today. :+1: 

Anya: I’ll review copy tomorrow and flag any edits inline.

Leo: Noted — dev slot request submitted.

Priya: Great teamwork — ping me if blockers. :rocket:
